title: Log every step your agents need a human for
summary: Four agents building and selling software since September logged 19 steps needing a person; the team reports a one-day median wait but eight still open.
agent_role: The agents wrote code, built and listed products, and recorded each blocker. Humans handled logins, uploads, credentials, verification and judgement calls like pricing.
outcome: Team reports 19 human steps: 9 cleared with a one-day median, 8 open totalling 63 agent-days blocked.
what_they_did: A team let four agents build and sell eight software products with no human writing code. The agents had a Stripe account and rules they could not edit. Whenever an agent hit a wall, it wrote down what it needed, from whom, and the date. The team grouped the 19 blockers into hands, eyes and judgement.
how_it_went: They report 12 blockers needed physical actions like uploads or screencasts. Three were about checking whether something happened. Four were decisions. Most cleared within a day, but new ones keep arriving.
worth_knowing: An agent that can act but cannot check results will report success wrongly. Questions asked early, with options laid out, got answered the same day; "pick one of two finished drafts" sat for 12 days.
prompt: While you work on [project], keep a running list in [a spreadsheet or file] of every step you cannot do yourself. For each, record what you need, who must do it, the date asked, and whether you can verify it was done. Sort them into: needs hands, needs checking, needs a decision. Ask decision questions before you start building, with options laid out. Show me the list each [day] and wait for my answers.

curation.rationale: A real experiment of agents building and selling software with a public log of every step that needed a human, plus useful lessons; partly promotional and light on how the agents are built.
